events.text: The council gathers. Mission 1 begins.
Zara proposes Zara, Elena. I want a team I can trust for Mission 1. I am including myself and Elena, who has not raised my suspicions, while avoiding players I currently distrust.

I am keeping my proposal of Zara and Elena. With only two seats, I want a team I can personally vouch for: I know my own card, and Elena has not raised the kind of concern that Maya and Priya have for me. Amara remains less clear to me, so I am not adding her to this first team. I understand some will want more evidence, but Mission 1 is exactly when we should avoid seats I currently distrust. If anyone has a concrete reason Elena is unsafe, state it; otherwise vote yes on Zara and Elena.

Zara, I want to respond to your reasoning directly. You said Elena has not raised your suspicions while Maya and Priya have. That logic concerns me — under your own standard, absence of suspicion is not the same as positive evidence of trustworthiness, and in a two-seat team the second seat carries half the risk of the whole mission. Elena has been quiet, but quiet players have never once been the reason a mission fails; a single Fail card from someone on the team is what sinks us, and Elena has done nothing to demonstrate commitment to good.

I also notice that both you and I were left off, which means the pair you proposed is entirely made up of players who cannot be tested against your judgment of the rest of us. That is precisely the setup where a single misread decides Mission 1, and with only two seats we get no redundancy at all.

Priya has at least engaged with the table and articulated positions; silence is not a contribution. I am not asking anyone to take my word on trust alone, but I am asking Zara a direct question: given that we cannot spare a seat, why is Priya the one excluded when Elena has offered us nothing beyond a clean record of not speaking badly of anyone? I would rather see Priya in the second seat than Elena, and I would like Zara to state which of the two she actually has positive reasons to trust, because that is the only basis on which this vote should be decided.

Maya, I will answer your direct question. My positive reason for Elena over Priya is not that Elena has spoken more; it is that I have a concrete concern about Priya’s positioning and none about Elena’s. I already said I distrust Maya and Priya. I know my own card, so the second seat must be someone I do not currently suspect. Elena has not lobbied to replace a teammate with someone I distrust, and she has not given me a specific reason to exclude her. Priya has not offered me a reason to trust her enough to put her on a two-seat Mission 1 team, and your argument that I should prefer Priya because she has engaged does not overcome that. Engagement is not proof of loyalty; a seat is. I am keeping Zara and Elena. Maya, if you have concrete evidence that Elena is unsafe, state that evidence directly; otherwise I ask you to vote yes on the team I can vouch for.

Elena, you hold the second seat on this team and you have not said a single word this discussion. I want to be direct about why that matters. On a two-person mission there is no redundancy: one Fail card from either of you sinks us, and silence has never once failed a mission, but it has also never once kept one safe. Absence of suspicion is not positive evidence, and I said that earlier and I still hold it.

So let me put my position on the table, and put a specific question to you and to Amara, because Amara has also stayed silent so far.

Here is the standard I am applying. Priya has actually engaged with this table — she has stated positions, engaged with others, and made herself a participant. Elena has offered the table nothing except a clean record of not accusing anyone. If we are choosing the second seat between a player who has taken a position and a player who has taken none, engagement has to count for something, and it currently counts in Priya's favor.

Elena, here is my direct question, and I want a direct answer, not reassurance: is there anything in Priya's behavior here — her positioning, her arguments, who she has agreed with and who she has not — that indicates to you that Priya is Evil? Amara, the same question to you: do you have a reason to think Priya is Evil? I am asking because I do not need to be right about Elena; I need to know whether anyone at this table has a positive reason to suspect Priya.

If one of you can state such a reason, state it plainly, and I will accept Priya staying off the team immediately — I will also say clearly that I never claimed Priya was good on evidence. I only claimed she has done the work of engaging while Elena has not. If neither of you has a reason, then my position is that Zara should revise this to Zara and Priya, and I would rather spend a seat on someone who has taken a position than on someone who has taken none.

Zara, I am not asking you to reassure me about your own card. I am asking whether Elena has given you anything positive — any argument, any position — because your stated reason for excluding Priya was Priya's positioning, and Elena has never made a positioning argument to anyone, including you. If Elena cannot answer the question about Priya, then the case for excluding Priya is a case about Priya, and not about Elena at all.

Maya, thank you for putting the question directly to me — I will answer it honestly. No, I do not have positive evidence that Priya is Evil, and I would rather admit that than manufacture suspicion to make you comfortable. I also want to be precise: I never accused Priya. The player who named Priya as someone she distrusts is Zara, and Zara has given the table her reasoning for that.

What I want the table to notice is the shape of your argument. You have said you do not need to be right about me. That means your case for removing me rests entirely on a single signal — that I have spoken less than Priya. I have been quiet because this is my first time hearing all of you, and I do not think a first impression earned by talking the fastest is worth much on a two-seat mission where one wrong seat decides everything. If silence is the strongest evidence against me, the accusation is thin, and I would rather be honestly quiet than loudly wrong.

So here is the specific point I want you to answer, Maya. Zara has stated plainly that she distrusts Priya's positioning, and you have given the table no reason to think Zara's read is mistaken — only that Priya engages more than I do. You are asking the leader to swap out a teammate she trusts for one she currently suspects. What is your specific reason to believe Zara's distrust of Priya is wrong? If you have one, state it and I will listen seriously. If you do not, then your argument is really that quiet players should be penalized, and I do not think we should vote a trusted seat off a two-person team on that basis.

Elena, you asked me a direct question and I owe you a direct answer, so here it is: I have no specific reason to believe Zara's read of Priya is wrong, and I will not manufacture one now. But you did not actually answer the question I put to you, Maya's question was whether Priya has done anything that indicates she is Evil, and your answer was that you have no positive evidence either way. That is the honest answer, and I appreciate it, but notice what it means for the table: the case against Priya has now been stated twice by the person making it, and no one — not you, not Amara — has produced a single concrete action by Priya that indicates Evil.

I set myself a condition earlier: if anyone could state a reason to suspect Priya, I would accept Priya staying off this team immediately. That condition has not been met. By my own standard, Priya is eligible for the second seat, and I am not going to be the person who quietly abandons it now that it costs me.

Elena, you framed your case as being about volume of speech, and I want to push back on that once more, precisely. This is Mission 1, there are two seats, and one Fail card decides it. A player who has never taken a position on any other player at this table is not a player who has been cleared — she is a player who has been untested. Your own words were that you have been quiet because this is your first time hearing all of us. Silence is not a reason to be seated on a two-person mission, and it is not a reason to vote a seat off one either. If Zara's genuine concern is Priya's positioning, then the way to resolve that concern is to hear Priya's position and test it, not to replace her with someone who has not offered a position to anyone.

So I am asking the table to consider that we have no basis for Priya and no basis for Elena, and that a second seat with no evidence behind it is a coin flip, while a second seat occupied by someone who has actually engaged carries at least the possibility of being tested.

Priya, I am asking you directly to answer for yourself: state your case for the second seat, and tell this table whether you have any concrete concern about Zara or about Elena that you have been holding back. The leader is not obliged to include you, but she is obliged to hear you, and I would rather this table vote on positions than on volume.

Zara, if you keep Elena, I want you to say on the record that the reason is that she has never been challenged, not that Priya has been shown to be unsafe.

Maya, while I appreciate you arguing for active engagement, I want to be clear that I am not desperately lobbying for a seat on Mission 1 just to be on it. My priority is ensuring we pass missions and get reliable information.

What does concern me, however, is Zara's immediate and definitive certainty right out of the gate. In her very first statements, Zara declared that she specifically distrusted Maya and me, later citing a 'concrete concern about Priya's positioning.' But Zara, you stated that suspicion before I had spoken a single word or taken any action at this table.

Zara, my direct question to you is: what specific positioning or action of mine prior to your proposal gave you that concrete concern, given that the game had barely begun?

If there was no actual basis, then creating an immediate divide and preemptively blacklisting me feels completely unfounded. I'd like you to explain that reasoning directly.

Priya, you are right to press me on that, and I will correct my own wording: I did not have a specific prior action of yours to point to when I first proposed. I should not have called it 'concrete concern about your positioning' before you had spoken. What I had was a strategic read of the table, not a piece of evidence I can lay out as if you had done something. I will not invent one now.

That correction does not make you the safer second seat. Since the proposal, Maya has built a sustained case to swap Elena for you, while you have framed your own case mainly around my initial certainty. Elena, by contrast, answered the question put to her directly and admitted she had no evidence against you rather than manufacturing it. On a two-seat Mission 1, I am weighing who has given me a stable basis to trust them, and I am keeping Elena.

Maya, you asked me to say on the record whether I keep Elena because she has never been challenged rather than because Priya is unsafe. I will say this plainly: I am not claiming Priya has been proven unsafe by public evidence. I am claiming that I have no positive reason to seat Priya on this team, and that Elena’s direct answer is a better basis than a swap driven by volume of speech. My team remains Zara and Elena.

I am Amara, and I have no information beyond my own Loyal Servant role, so I am judging only what has been said at this table. Zara, you have now conceded that you had no concrete basis for distrusting Priya when you first proposed, and Elena has said she has no evidence against Priya. That means neither the exclusion of Priya nor the inclusion of Elena rests on evidence yet, and I do not think either should be decided on who has spoken more. Elena, I am asking you directly: Zara's initial distrust of Maya and Priya came before either of them had acted at this table. Do you find that reasoning sound, and do you have any concrete reason to think Zara's distrust was grounded in something observed? I will weigh my vote on your answer and on any concrete reasons offered.

Amara, you asked me directly whether Zara's initial distrust was grounded in something observed, and the honest answer is no — Zara has already conceded she had no specific prior action to point to. I think it was the right call for her to correct that openly rather than defend a claim she could not support.

But I want to separate two things. Zara's opening read was imprecise; that is on the table now. What matters for this vote is who has demonstrated trustworthiness since the proposal began. Zara has held a consistent position under sustained pressure. I answered Maya's question about Priya honestly rather than manufacturing a case. Neither Priya nor I has done anything that indicates Evil, and I am not claiming otherwise.

What I am saying is that on a two-seat team, I would rather the second seat be someone who has faced direct questioning and answered it than someone who has been largely untested at this table. That is not a claim that Priya is Evil — it is a claim that silence and engagement are not equivalent when one Fail card decides the mission.

Maya asked Priya directly to state her case for the second seat and to tell the table whether she has any concrete concern about Zara or about Elena. I would like to hear that answer before anyone votes.

Elena, to answer your question directly: I am not making a desperate bid to force myself into the second seat on Mission 1. My priority is simply that we field a team we can understand and trust, whether I am on it or not. I do not have concrete evidence that you are Evil, Elena, nor am I manufacturing any. My concern from the beginning was strictly about Zara's immediate, unprompted certainty in blacklisting Maya and me before anyone had spoken. Zara has now admitted that her concrete concern was not based on anything observed, but was merely a strategic read. While I respect her honesty in acknowledging that mistake, it still leaves this proposal resting entirely on Zara's unsupported intuition. We have an unvetted two-person team where the justification for Elena over anyone else is essentially that Elena was quiet and did not trigger Zara's gut feeling. Amara, you pointed out earlier that neither Elena's inclusion nor my exclusion is backed by evidence. Given that Zara's foundation for this pairing has dissolved into an admitted guess, where do you stand on approving this team versus letting the proposal pass to the next leader to see fresh combinations?

Priya, you asked where I stand, so here it is. Zara has conceded that her initial distrust of Maya and Priya was a strategic read rather than anything observed, and Elena has said she has no evidence against Priya. That leaves this pairing without a concrete basis for either seat. I cannot see a positive reason to approve Zara and Elena, and I do not think a team should pass on a read its own proposer has withdrawn. I will vote to reject unless someone can point to an observed action that supports Elena or justifies excluding Priya. Zara, I would like you to say whether anything you have seen since the proposal, rather than before it, changes your reasoning. I am not claiming Zara or Elena is Evil. I simply have no evidence yet that either is trustworthy with a Fail card on a two-seat mission. The next leader should propose a team built on observed behavior.

Amara, you said you will vote to reject unless someone points to observed behavior that supports Elena or justifies excluding Priya. I want to respond directly to that standard, because I think it sets a bar that no Mission 1 proposal can meet.

We are on the first mission with five players who have had no prior games together. There is no observed behavior yet — not for me, not for Priya, not for Zara, not for anyone. If we reject every team that lacks observed evidence, we will reject five teams and hand Evil the game without ever playing one. That is not a standard for approving a team; it is a standard for ensuring none ever passes.

What we do have is the behavior of this discussion itself. Zara corrected her own overreach when Priya challenged her. I answered Maya's question about Priya honestly instead of manufacturing suspicion. Neither of those is proof of loyalty in the abstract, but they are what we can observe right now, and they are the only currency available on Mission 1.

I also want to name what happens if we reject this proposal. Leadership passes to Maya, who has spent this entire discussion arguing that Priya should take my seat. If the team is rejected, we are likely to see a Maya-led proposal that may include Priya, Amara, or others — and none of those combinations have more evidence behind them than this one. Rejecting does not move us toward a team with observed support; it moves us to a new leader with the same absence of evidence.

Amara, I have a direct question for you. You said you are not claiming Zara or Elena is Evil. If your concern is the lack of evidence rather than a specific suspicion, is the real issue that no Mission 1 team can satisfy your standard — or is there something about this specific pairing, beyond the absence of observed behavior, that makes you willing to risk a rejection?

Elena, you asked whether the real issue is that no Mission 1 team can meet my standard, or something specific to this pairing. The honest answer is both. No one has observed behavior yet, so I should not hold this team to a bar no team can clear. My concern about this pairing is narrower. Zara's only stated reason for choosing Elena over Priya was her distrust of Priya, and Zara has now said that distrust was a strategic read rather than anything observed. That leaves Elena's inclusion resting on her silence and on her direct answer to Maya. I count that answer as a small positive, but it is a response to a question, not evidence of loyalty. Priya's point that the pairing has lost its stated basis still stands. I am not accusing Zara or Elena of being Evil. I am saying the observed record does not give me a reason to prefer this pair over another. Zara, if you have a reason for Elena that you formed from what you have seen since the proposal, state it and I will weigh it seriously. Elena, I also accept that rejecting this team moves us to a new leader with the same thin evidence, and I do not want rejection to become the default. My vote remains open to yes if Zara gives an observed reason.

Amara makes a very sensible point. While Elena is right that Mission 1 naturally begins with limited data, that does not mean we are obligated to rubber-stamp the very first proposal when its core foundation was openly acknowledged as an unsupported guess. In a five-player game, we have up to five proposal attempts before any danger of a forced hammer. Using our early votes to observe how different players construct teams and handle scrutiny is one of the only tools Good has to generate reliable information before cards are cast. Since Zara's pairing rests purely on arbitrary selection and gives the table no real accountability, letting leadership rotate to Maya provides a fresh perspective and more observable behavior to evaluate. For those reasons, I agree with Amara and will be voting to reject this proposal.

Zara confirms Zara, Elena. I am keeping Zara and Elena. I corrected my earlier overstatement, but Elena has answered direct questions consistently, while no observed action gives me a positive reason to replace her on this two-seat Mission 1 team.
Team rejected (2 approve, 3 reject).

Maya proposes Maya, Priya. As leader I am putting myself on the team, and I am taking the second seat with Priya. My reasoning for Priya is that she is the player who has actually engaged at this table and has been least examined — everyone has theorized about her but nobody has tested her, and on a two-person mission that untested slot is where a mistake gets made. I have no concrete concern about Priya, and as leader I have no seat to waste on a player I cannot vouch for. Pairing Priya with myself also means the second seat is not a gamble on a player who has said nothing at all. I would rather we run a team we both understand than keep delaying for evidence that Mission 1 cannot produce.

I will vote no on Maya and Priya. Maya’s proposal repeats the same flaw she criticized in Zara’s team: it rests on a strategic read rather than an observed reason to trust the second seat. Maya argued that Priya was untested and that untested was not cleared; she now seats Priya without pointing to any action since the last vote that makes Priya safe on a two-seat mission. That is not a team built on evidence; it is a team built on the same absence of evidence, only with different names. Priya also said she was not lobbying for Mission 1 and agreed that Zara’s unsupported pairing should be rejected so leadership could rotate. Now Priya is on the replacement team without any new observed basis being offered. I am not persuaded by rotation alone if the next leader simply puts herself and the previously untested player forward. Priya, you said you were not desperate for the seat and that unsupported proposals should be rejected; what observed action since Zara’s rejection justifies your inclusion now, beyond the fact that Maya chose you? I would rather hear that answered than vote for a pair whose only public justification is that Maya is the leader and Priya has spoken.

Zara, I will answer your question directly, but I want to correct your framing first. I said I was not lobbying for a seat on Mission 1, and that remains entirely true. I did not ask Maya to propose me, nor am I insisting that this team must go through with me on it. As leader, Maya put forward the pairing she felt best about, which is her prerogative to propose for table discussion.

To your question about what observed action justifies my inclusion: what we have observed over the previous round is how players conduct themselves under scrutiny. You opened the game by definitively blacklisting two players before any discussion happened, and when pressed, you conceded it was an unsupported strategic read. Despite admitting the foundation was absent, you refused to adjust or explore any alternatives. Maya, on the other hand, actively questioned the premise, pushed for accountability, and sought to evaluate players based on real engagement.

That said, I want to be consistent with the principles I laid out earlier. I supported rejecting the first proposal because it rested on an admitted guess, and I do not expect the table to apply a double standard just because I happen to be on this draft. I have no personal attachment to being on Mission 1; my priority is fielding a team that Good can genuinely rally behind. If the table feels that Maya and Priya does not provide sufficient confidence or that testing another combination offers better clarity, I am completely supportive of Maya adjusting the lineup.

Amara, you were clear on the last proposal that you wanted to see leadership rotate and assess fresh combinations rather than rubber-stamp an arbitrary guess. Now that Maya has put forward Maya and Priya, where do you stand on this pairing, and do you feel this proposal addresses your concerns or should Maya consider revising it?

Priya, you asked where I stand, so here is my position on Maya and Priya. I have no information beyond my Loyal Servant role, so I am judging only what has been said and done at this table. Maya's stated reason is that Priya has engaged but has not been tested, and that Maya has no concrete concern about her. That is not a reason to suspect Priya. Priya's conduct has been consistent: she challenged Zara's read when it had no observed basis, and she has not pushed for a seat. That is a small positive I can actually observe. My concern is narrower. Maya's proposal also rests on no observed action by Priya since the last vote, only on Priya having spoken and on Maya wanting to test her. I rejected Zara's team because its basis was withdrawn, and I should apply the same standard here. Priya, you said unsupported proposals should be rejected so leadership can rotate, and you are now on a team proposed on that same basis. Can you explain why you would accept a seat you earlier argued should be rejected, and whether you have any observed reason to trust Maya's second-seat choice beyond her wish to test you? I am not accusing you of anything. If your answer shows that you accept this team as the best available option and have no reason to suspect Maya, I am leaning toward yes. I will vote on your answer and on any observed reason offered.

Amara, to answer your questions directly:

First, on why I would accept this seat: my objection to Zara's proposal was not simply that the second seat was untested. My objection was that Zara justified excluding me based on a claimed 'concrete concern about my positioning' that she subsequently admitted had zero basis before I had spoken a single word, and then refused to reconsider when that foundation dissolved. On Mission 1, no one has historical data, but the process matters. Rejecting Zara’s proposal was about holding a leader accountable for arbitrary blacklisting, not about establishing an impossible rule that every team must be rejected until round five.

Second, regarding why I trust Maya’s choice: Maya has been completely transparent about her reasoning rather than claiming false certainty. She stepped up, took accountability by placing herself on the team as leader, and engaged directly and constructively with everyone's points. Her decision to include me isn't based on a manufactured read or ungrounded suspicion; it is an open proposal that both of us have to answer for at the table. I have not observed anything evasive or manipulative from Maya—her arguments have been consistent, principled, and open to scrutiny.

We will never get infallible proof on Mission 1 without actually running a team. What we have here is a leader taking full responsibility for her lineup and an open, accountable record of discussion. I believe this pairing is our best available option to move forward and gain real mission data, which is why I support it.

Zara: I will vote no on Maya and Priya. This is not a reversal of my correction: I accept I had no observed basis for distrusting Priya when I first spoke. But the public record now gives me one. Priya argued that Zara's pairing should be rejected because it rested on an admitted guess, and she explicitly said she was not lobbying for Mission 1. She now supports a team whose only justification is that Maya, as leader, wants to test her. Maya spent the previous discussion saying untested is not cleared, then gave the second seat to the most-discussed untested player without pointing to any observed action by Priya. That is the same flaw with different names. Priya, you asked Amara to judge you on process. Your answer to Amara was that Maya's openness and accountability make this team acceptable, but openness is not evidence that either seat is safe on a two-seat mission where one Fail card loses. You also said you would accept Maya revising the lineup. I want a direct answer: name one observed action by Maya or by you since the last vote that makes this exact pairing safer than Zara and Elena, rather than simply a different unsupported guess. If you cannot, the table should reject and let leadership rotate again. I am voting no.

Zara, to answer your question directly: the observed action that makes this pairing different is not that Maya or I have proven ourselves through completed missions—that is impossible before Mission 1 runs—but how we have conducted ourselves under public scrutiny. When you proposed your team, you justified excluding me with a claimed 'concrete concern' that you admitted had zero basis, yet you doubled down and refused to consider any alternative. In contrast, Maya has been transparent about her criteria, stepped up to take direct responsibility as leader, and engaged every critique head-on without manufacturing false certainty.

Furthermore, I have answered every direct question put to me openly and consistently, without evading or desperately lobbying for a seat. That willingness to be examined and held accountable in front of the table is the only observable behavioral evidence Good can generate before cards are cast.

You argue that because we lack prior mission data, this is merely 'the same flaw with different names.' But by that standard, no leader could ever propose a valid team on Mission 1, because every combination initially lacks track records. The meaningful distinction is between an entrenched selection rooted in an admitted guess versus a leader taking ownership of an open, tested dialogue.

Amara, you noted earlier that you were leaning toward yes if my reasoning showed this pairing as the best available path forward without reason to suspect Maya. Does this distinction between accountability under scrutiny and arbitrary selection satisfy your threshold for moving forward with Mission 1, or do you have any remaining concerns before we proceed to a vote?

Priya, thank you for a direct answer. I accept that your objection to Zara's team was about process: Zara excluded you on a read she later admitted had no observed basis, and you challenged that openly. That is observed conduct, and it is the reason I am willing to consider this pairing at all. I also accept that Mission 1 cannot offer track records. Where I remain unconvinced is the reasoning behind this specific seat. Maya's stated basis is that you are untested and she wants to test you. Openness about a leader's reasoning is not the same as evidence about a Fail card, and accountability under scrutiny shows how you argue, not how you will act on a mission. So my vote is not settled. Maya, you have said you have no concrete concern about Priya and that the seat is for testing. Can you name one observed action by Priya in this game, beyond engaging and answering questions, that you count as a positive? If you cannot, would you consider revising the second seat before the vote? I am not accusing you of anything. I want this team to rest on something observed, and I lean toward yes if your answer gives me that.

Amara, you asked me directly for one observed action by Priya that I count as a positive, and whether I would revise the second seat. I will answer both plainly, and I will name what I am really voting on here. First, the observed action. Priya's conduct across this table has been consistent in a way I can actually point to. When Zara excluded her on a 'concrete concern about positioning' before Priya had spoken a single word, Priya did not retaliate, did not manufacture a counter-accusation, and did not lobby for a seat. She challenged the reasoning, demanded it be grounded, and when the leader conceded it was not, she said plainly that she had no personal stake in being on Mission 1 and that the table should decide on principles rather than on who wanted the seat. That is a player putting the mission outcome above her own position, and it is something I saw happen, not something I inferred from silence. Second, on revision: no. I am not revising the second seat, and I want to be honest about why rather than strategic. My concern about Priya, when I have one, is about what she does on a mission, not about whether she is articulate. No leader can produce a track record on Mission 1, and no table can either. What we can observe is conduct under scrutiny, and Priya has answered every question put to her directly, without evasion and without false certainty, while accepting a seat she had argued was unjustified only minutes earlier. Zara had a team on the table with no observed basis at all and refused to reconsider it when its foundation was withdrawn. I am not going to build a team on that standard and then penalize a player for having more of a record than my own proposal does. Zara, you have asked twice for an observed action that makes Maya and Priya safer than Zara and Elena, and you have told the table you will vote no either way. So let me answer that in the same register you used. If the bar is that Priya must be shown safe, she cannot be shown it, and neither can Elena — but Elena has offered no position to anyone until she was directly questioned, while Priya has taken a consistent, accountable position on every question asked of her. If the bar is that I must prove my own seat, I am the leader and I am answerable for it at the table; that is what taking the first seat means. I will not swap Priya for a player who has said nothing, because silence has never yet protected anyone from a Fail card on a two-seat mission. Amara, you said you would weigh my answer and lean yes if it gave you an observed reason. I have given you one: Priya chose the mission over her own seat, and she has been consistent and examinable throughout. My team remains Maya

I will vote no on Maya and Priya. This proposal repeats the defect I identified in the first team: it seats the second player on no observed basis. Maya spent the previous discussion arguing that untested is not cleared, then chose Priya because Priya is untested and Maya wants to test her. Priya argued that Zara's pairing should be rejected because it rested on an admitted guess, and said she was not lobbying for Mission 1; she now supports a team whose only public justification is that the leader chose her. Openness under scrutiny shows how a player argues, not whether that player will put Success on a two-seat mission where one Fail loses. Amara, you asked for an observed positive, and Maya's answer described Priya's conduct in discussion, not anything about mission safety. That is not enough to make this pair safer than the team the table just rejected. I accept my earlier correction, but accepting an error does not convert an unsupported second seat into a supported one. Amara, do you treat conduct under scrutiny as sufficient evidence for a mission seat, or will you require a basis closer to mission safety? If the latter, vote no.

Zara, I do not treat conduct under scrutiny as sufficient evidence for a mission seat on its own. I said as much when I pressed Priya for an observed action, and Maya's answer mostly described discussion conduct. But no player on Mission 1 has evidence closer to mission safety, Good included, so I cannot require proof of safety without rejecting every possible team and handing Evil the game. My standard is narrower: the proposer's reason for the seat should be specific, checkable, and not built on a read the proposer has withdrawn. Maya's reason is thin. She has no concrete concern about Priya and is seating her to test her, and I will say so plainly. Still, Priya has consistently challenged a read that had no observed basis, and Zara has conceded that her own basis for excluding Priya was unsupported. Against that, the only alternative on the table is the team already rejected. I lean yes on Maya and Priya, though not with confidence, and I will vote on whether the reasoning holds up after the reveal.
